role: Pre-ranking source-section evidence probes for the separately written transfer questions, not exhaustive answer labels

cases.facts: Tie permanently bonds tied nodes for the simulation; ordinary separation/sliding is not that constraint's behavior. Distinguish initially untied nodes and element deletion exceptions.
Kinematic constrains selected motion to rigid motion; distributing relates reference motion to an average and permits deformation within the coupling region.
Added mass increases inertial forces; excessive scaling can change the solution even in a nominally quasi-static run.

sections: Choosing between Regular and Hybrid Elements
cases.facts: Near incompressibility makes a displacement-only pressure solution sensitive; hybrid uses independently interpolated pressure stress.
Out-of-plane normal and shear strains vanish; thickness-direction stress need not vanish, as thermal expansion example shows.

sections: Choosing between Full- and Reduced-Integration Elements
cases.facts: One-point integration can permit distortions with zero computed strain at the integration point; hourglass control addresses uncontrolled distortion and is not a substitute for adequate mesh.

sections: Extrapolation and Interpolation of Element Output Variables
cases.facts: Element shape functions extrapolate integration-point values; extrapolated values can be less accurate in steep stress gradients. Read actual paragraph, not just parent-page hit.

sections: Estimating the Stable Time Increment Size
cases.facts: Small characteristic element length and wave speed limit a stable increment; global stability estimation may reduce sensitivity later in the step.
